def _strip_markup(text: str) -> str:
    prev = None
    while prev != text:
        prev = text
        text = _MARKDOWN_BOLD.sub(r"\1", text)
    text = _MARKDOWN_ITALIC.sub(r"\1", text)
    return text


def _fold_ascii(text: str) -> str:
    return (
        unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text)
        .encode("ascii", "ignore")
        .decode("ascii")
    )


def _normalize_surface_no_desc(answer: str) -> str:
    """Formatting/wrapper cleanup that never drops descriptor words."""
    text = _strip_markup(answer or "")
    text = _fold_ascii(text)
    text = _EDGE_QUOTES.sub("", text)
    text = _LEADING_ANSWER_LABEL.sub("", text)
    text = _TRAILING_PUNCT.sub("", text)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()


def normalize_surface(answer: str) -> str:
    """Backwards-compatible surface normalizer (keeps old always-strip mode)."""
    text = _normalize_surface_no_desc(answer)
    text = _UNIVERSITY_SUFFIX.sub("", text)
    text = _LEGAL_SUFFIX.sub("", text)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()


def _descriptor_variants(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Return [full, ...stripped] variants for trailing descriptors."""
    variants = [text]
    t = _UNIVERSITY_SUFFIX.sub("", text).strip()
    if t and t != text:
        variants.append(t)
    t = _LEGAL_SUFFIX.sub("", text).strip()
    if t and t != text:
        variants.append(t)
    t = _LEGAL_SUFFIX.sub("", _UNIVERSITY_SUFFIX.sub("", text)).strip()
    if t and t != text and t not in variants:
        variants.append(t)
    return variants


def _normalize_surface_contextual(answer: str, context: str) -> str:
    """Surface cleanup that strips descriptors only when the context says so.

    If the full answer (e.g. ``Stanford University``) is already a contiguous
    context span, keep it.  If it is not, prefer the shortest stripped variant
    that is supported by the context.  Only when nothing is supported do we
    fall back to the old always-strip behaviour.
    """
    base = _normalize_surface_no_desc(answer)
    if not base:
        return base
    if not context:
        text = _UNIVERSITY_SUFFIX.sub("", base)
        text = _LEGAL_SUFFIX.sub("", text)
        return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()

    variants = _descriptor_variants(base)
    if _is_supported_span(base, context):
        return base
    for variant in variants[1:]:
        if _is_supported_span(variant, context):
            return variant

    base_cmp = _cmp_text(base)
    for _clue, ans in _parse_qa_cells(context):
        if base_cmp and base_cmp == _cmp_text(ans):
            return base
    return variants[-1] if len(variants) > 1 else base


def _cmp_text(text: str) -> str:
    """Comparison normalization aligned with the QA grader."""
    text = _fold_ascii(text).lower()
    text = "".join(ch for ch in text if ch.isalnum() or ch.isspace())
    text = re.sub(r"\b(?:a|an|the)\b", " ", text)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()


def _content_tokens(text: str) -> list[str]:
    out: list[str] = []
    for tok in _cmp_text(text).split():
        if tok in _STOP:
            continue
        out.append(tok)
    return out


def _split_sentences(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Split text into sentences without breaking on abbreviation periods.

    A period inside ``U.S.`` or ``Ph.D.`` is followed by a lowercase word, so a
    sentence boundary requires the next non-space character to be uppercase, a
    digit, or a tag/opening punctuation marker.
    """
    parts = _SENTENCE_SPLIT.split(text)
    return [part.strip() for part in parts if part.strip()]


def _split_task(task: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Return (question, context) from the full wrapped task prompt."""
    question = task
    context = task

    qm = list(re.finditer(r"(?im)^\s*(?:question|task)\s*:\s*(.*)$", task))
    if qm:
        question = qm[-1].group(1).strip()

    cm = re.search(r"(?is)Context:\n(.*?)\n\nQuestion:\n(.*)$", task)
    if cm:
        context = cm.group(1).strip()
        question = cm.group(2).strip()
    else:
        cidx = task.find("Context:")
        if cidx >= 0:
            context = task[cidx + len("Context:"):].strip()
            qidx = context.rfind("\nQuestion:")
            if qidx >= 0:
                question = context[qidx + len("\nQuestion:"):].strip()
                context = context[:qidx].strip()
            else:
                qidx = context.rfind("\nquestion:")
                if qidx >= 0:
                    question = context[qidx + len("\nquestion:"):].strip()
                    context = context[:qidx].strip()
    return question, context


def _parse_docs(context: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    docs: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for part in re.split(r"\[DOC\]", context, flags=re.IGNORECASE):
        part = part.strip()
        if not part:
            continue
        tm = re.search(r"\[TLE\]\s*(.*?)(?:\n|\[PAR\])", part, re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
        title = tm.group(1).strip() if tm else ""
        pm = re.search(r"\[PAR\]\s*(.*)$", part, re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
        text = pm.group(1).strip() if pm else part
        docs.append((title, text))
    return docs


def _clean_qa_field(field: str) -> str:
    field = _TAG_ANYWHERE.sub(" ", field)
    field = re.sub(r"\s+(?:right|wrong)\s*:.*$", "", field, flags=re.I | re.S)
    field = re.sub(r"\s+value\s*:.*$", "", field, flags=re.I | re.S)
    field = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", field).strip()
    return _TRAILING_PUNCT.sub("", field).strip()


def _terminal_end(text: str) -> bool:
    return bool(re.search(r"[.!?]['\")\]]?$", text.strip()))


def _parse_qa_cells(context: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Extract ``CLUE | ANSWER`` cells from [PAR] snippets, line by line.

    [PAR] blocks frequently contain several Q&A lines.  The old whole-block
    parser joined all lines and kept only the last two vertical-bar fields,
    which both discarded earlier cells and manufactured a bogus clue.  We now
    split physical lines, splice short wrap-lines onto the previous Q&A line,
    and take the final vertical bar of each logical line.
    """
    cells: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for doc in re.split(r"\[DOC\]", context, flags=re.IGNORECASE):
        pm = re.search(r"\[PAR\](.*)$", doc, flags=re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
        if not pm:
            continue
        par = pm.group(1)
        par = re.sub(r"\[(?:TLE|PAR|DOC)\]", " ", par, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
        par = par.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")
        lines = [ln.strip() for ln in par.split("\n") if ln.strip()]

        logical: list[str] = []
        for ln in lines:
            if "|" in ln:
                logical.append(ln)
            elif logical and not _terminal_end(logical[-1]):
                # Short wrap-line continuation of the previous Q&A cell.
                logical[-1] += " " + ln
            # else: prose line without a pipe; skip it intentionally.

        if not logical and "|" in re.sub(r"\s+", " ", par):
            logical = [re.sub(r"\s+", " ", par).strip()]

        for line in logical:
            if "|" not in line:
                continue
            fields = [f.strip() for f in line.split("|")]
            if len(fields) < 2:
                continue
            clue = " | ".join(fields[:-1]).strip()
            ans = _clean_qa_field(fields[-1])
            clue = _strip_markup(clue).strip()
            ans = _strip_markup(ans).strip()
            clue = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", clue).strip()
            ans = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", ans).strip()
            if not clue or not ans:
                continue
            if "..." in ans:
                continue
            if len(ans.split()) > 12:
                continue
            if _BAD_ANSWER.search(ans):
                continue
            if len(_content_tokens(clue)) < 2 or len(_content_tokens(ans)) < 1:
                continue
            cells.append((clue, ans))

    # De-duplicate identical normalized clue/answer pairs.
    seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
    out: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for clue, ans in cells:
        key = (_cmp_text(clue), _cmp_text(ans))
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        out.append((clue, ans))
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Similarity and retrieval
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _token_similarity(a: str, b: str) -> float:
    if a == b:
        return 1.0
    if len(a) < 4 or len(b) < 4:
        return 0.0
    return SequenceMatcher(None, a, b).ratio()


def _weighted_overlap(left: list[str], right: list[str]) -> float:
    if not left or not right:
        return 0.0
    used: set[int] = set()
    total = 0.0
    for tok in left:
        best_i = -1
        best_s = 0.0
        for i, other in enumerate(right):
            if i in used:
                continue
            s = _token_similarity(tok, other)
            if s > best_s:
                best_s = s
                best_i = i
        if best_i >= 0 and best_s > 0.72:
            total += best_s
            used.add(best_i)
    return total


def _clue_similarity(question: str, clue: str) -> float:
    qt = _content_tokens(question)
    ct = _content_tokens(clue)
    if not qt or not ct:
        return 0.0
    inter = _weighted_overlap(qt, ct)
    score = 2.0 * inter / (len(qt) + len(ct))
    q = _cmp_text(question)
    c = _cmp_text(clue)
    if len(c) >= 3 and c in q:
        score = max(score, 0.90)
    elif len(q) >= 3 and q in c:
        score = max(score, 0.80)
    return min(score, 1.0)


def _bm25_score(
    query_tokens: list[str],
    clue_tokens: list[str],
    idf: dict[str, float],
    avgdl: float,
    k1: float = 1.6,
    b: float = 0.75,
) -> float:
    if not query_tokens or not clue_tokens:
        return 0.0
    dl = len(clue_tokens)
    tf: dict[str, int] = {}
    for tok in clue_tokens:
        tf[tok] = tf.get(tok, 0) + 1
    score = 0.0
    for tok in query_tokens:
        if tok not in idf or tok not in tf:
            continue
        f = tf[tok]
        denom = f + k1 * (1.0 - b + b * dl / max(1.0, avgdl))
        score += idf[tok] * (f * (k1 + 1.0)) / denom
    return score


def _bm25_top_cells(
    question: str, context: str, limit: int = 8
) -> list[tuple[float, float, str, str]]:
    """Rank parsed Q&A cells by BM25/IDF plus token-overlap similarity.

    Returns ``(combined_score, clue_similarity, clue, answer)`` tuples sorted
    by combined score.
    """
    cells = _parse_qa_cells(context)
    if not cells:
        return []

    corpus = [_content_tokens(clue) for clue, _ in cells]
    n_docs = len(corpus)
    df: dict[str, int] = {}
    for toks in corpus:
        for tok in set(toks):
            df[tok] = df.get(tok, 0) + 1
    avgdl = sum(len(toks) for toks in corpus) / max(1, n_docs)
    idf = {
        tok: math.log(1.0 + (n_docs - df[tok] + 0.5) / (df[tok] + 0.5))
        for tok in df
    }

    qt = _content_tokens(question)
    q = _cmp_text(question)
    scored: list[tuple[float, float, str, str]] = []
    for (clue, ans), ct in zip(cells, corpus):
        bm = _bm25_score(qt, ct, idf, avgdl)
        sim = _clue_similarity(question, clue)
        bonus = 0.0
        c = _cmp_text(clue)
        if len(c) >= 4 and c in q:
            bonus += 0.35
        elif len(q) >= 4 and q in c:
            bonus += 0.20
        if 1 <= len(_content_tokens(ans)) <= 6:
            bonus += 0.05
        scored.append((bm + 1.6 * sim + bonus, sim, clue, ans))
    scored.sort(key=lambda item: item[0], reverse=True)
    return scored[:limit]


def _top_doc_lines(
    question: str, context: str, limit: int = 5
) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Return short (title, first sentence) snippets most relevant to the question."""
    docs = _parse_docs(context)
    if not docs:
        return []
    q_tokens = set(_content_tokens(question))
    if not q_tokens:
        return []
    scored: list[tuple[float, str, str]] = []
    for title, text in docs:
        doc_tokens = set(_content_tokens(title + " " + text))
        score = len(q_tokens & doc_tokens) / max(1, len(q_tokens))
        title_tokens = set(_content_tokens(title))
        score += 0.2 * len(q_tokens & title_tokens) / max(1, len(q_tokens))
        first = ""
        if text.strip():
            first = _split_sentences(text.strip())[0][:280]
        scored.append((score, title.strip(), first))
    scored.sort(key=lambda item: item[0], reverse=True)
    return [(title, first) for _score, title, first in scored[:limit] if title or first]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Deterministic category extraction
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _title_only(question: str) -> bool:
    return not re.search(
        r"\b(this|that|these|those|what|who|where|when|why|how|which|whose|"
        r"\bname\b|\bhe\b|\bshe\b|\bit\b|\bthey\b)\b",
        question,
        re.IGNORECASE,
    )


def _extract_category(question: str, context: str) -> str | None:
    """Best-effort category answer for bare-title / Jeopardy-style clues."""
    # "Mount X in Y" -> country following the known region Y.
    m = re.search(r"^Mount\s+.+?\bin\s+([A-Z][a-zA-Z]+(?:\s+[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+)*)", question)
    if m:
        region = m.group(1).strip()
        pat = re.compile(
            r"\b" + re.escape(region) + r"\s*,\s*([A-Z][a-zA-Z]+(?:\s+[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+)*)"
        )
        for sent in _split_sentences(context):
            mm = pat.search(sent)
            if mm:
                for tok in re.findall(r"[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+(?:\s+[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+)*", mm.group(1)):
                    if tok in _COUNTRIES:
                        return tok

    # "Home to ..." -> the state/country mentioned in the home/location sentence.
    if re.match(r"^Home\s+to", question, re.IGNORECASE):
        for sent in _split_sentences(context):
            if re.search(r"home\s+to|oldest|world", sent, re.IGNORECASE):
                for tok in re.findall(r"[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+(?:\s+[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+)*", sent):
                    if tok in _US_STATES or tok in _COUNTRIES:
                        return tok

    if not _title_only(question):
        return None

    qnorm = _cmp_text(question)
    if not qnorm:
        return None

    docs = _parse_docs(context)
    # Bare "X State Park" title -> the U.S. state named in a state-park
    # sentence that also mentions the park title.
    if re.search(r"\bstate\s+park\b", question, re.IGNORECASE):
        q_tokens = set(_content_tokens(question)) - {"state", "park"}
        for title, text in docs:
            for sent in _split_sentences(text):
                if "state park" not in sent.lower():
                    continue
                sent_tokens = set(_content_tokens(sent))
                if q_tokens and not (q_tokens & sent_tokens):
                    continue
                for tok in re.findall(r"[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+(?:\s+[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+)*", sent):
                    if tok in _US_STATES:
                        return tok

    # Bare company/weapon name -> nationality of the company from the context.
    for title, text in docs:
        t = _cmp_text(title)
        if not t:
            continue
        if qnorm in t or t in qnorm:
            m = re.search(
                r"\b(Italian|French|German|American|British|Japanese|Russian|"
                r"Spanish|Swiss|Swedish|Australian|Canadian|Chinese|Indian|"
                r"Korean|Mexican)\s+(?:firearms\s+manufacturing\s+)?company\b",
                text,
                re.IGNORECASE,
            )
            if m:
                return _NATIONALITY_COUNTRY.get(m.group(1).lower())
    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Deterministic answer reductions / repairs
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _abbrev_variants(answer: str, context: str) -> str:
    """Copy the context's preferred Mount/Mt., Saint/St., Fort/Ft. form."""
    pairs = (
        (r"^Mount\s+(.+)$", "Mt."),
        (r"^Saint\s+(.+)$", "St."),
        (r"^Fort\s+(.+)$", "Ft."),
    )
    text = answer
    for pat, abbr in pairs:
        m = re.match(pat, text, re.IGNORECASE)
        if m and re.search(r"\b" + re.escape(abbr) + r"\.?\s+" + re.escape(m.group(1)) + r"\b", context):
            text = abbr + ". " + m.group(1)
            break
    # Reverse direction: context prefers the spelled-out form.
    pairs_rev = (
        (r"^Mt\.\s+(.+)$", "Mount"),
        (r"^St\.\s+(.+)$", "Saint"),
        (r"^Ft\.\s+(.+)$", "Fort"),
    )
    for pat, full in pairs_rev:
        m = re.match(pat, text, re.IGNORECASE)
        if m and re.search(r"\b" + re.escape(full) + r"\.?\s+" + re.escape(m.group(1)) + r"\b", context):
            text = full + " " + m.group(1)
            break
    return text


def _apply_precision_repairs(question: str, context: str, answer: str) -> str:
    """Small pattern-based repairs that are safe for exact-match QA."""
    text = answer

    # "one of these" clues expect a singular category noun.
    if re.search(r"one\s+of\s+these", question, re.IGNORECASE) and re.search(
        r"s$", text
    ):
        if not re.search(r"ss$", text):
            singular = text[:-1]
            if _is_supported_span(singular, context) or re.search(
                r"\b" + re.escape(singular) + r"\b", context, re.IGNORECASE
            ):
                text = singular

    text = _abbrev_variants(text, context)

    # "Titanic (1997)" -> "Titanic".
    text = re.sub(
        r"\s*\(\s*(?:\d{4}|\d{4}\s*[-–]\s*\d{4})\s*\)\s*$",
        "",
        text,
    )

    # "Department of the X" -> "the X Department" when the context uses it.
    m = re.match(r"^Department\s+of\s+the\s+(.+)$", text, re.IGNORECASE)
    if m and re.search(r"\bdepartment\b", question, re.IGNORECASE):
        name = m.group(1).strip()
        pat = re.compile(r"\bthe\s+" + re.escape(name) + r"\s+Department\b", re.IGNORECASE)
        hit = pat.search(context)
        if hit:
            text = hit.group(0)

    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()


def _is_supported_span(answer: str, context: str) -> bool:
    """True when the answer is already a contiguous token span in the context."""
    a_tokens = _cmp_text(answer).split()
    c_tokens = _cmp_text(context).split()
    if not a_tokens:
        return False
    n = len(a_tokens)
    return any(c_tokens[i:i + n] == a_tokens for i in range(len(c_tokens) - n + 1))


def _cmp_span_token(tok: str) -> str:
    """Compare a raw token for exact-span restoration.

    This is like ``_cmp_text`` for one token, but it keeps leading articles so
    an answer such as ``The Hague`` can restore the article from the context
    instead of being reduced to ``Hague``.
    """
    c = _cmp_text(tok)
    if not c and _fold_ascii(tok).lower() in {"a", "an", "the"}:
        return _fold_ascii(tok).lower()
    return c


def _restore_exact_span(answer: str, context: str) -> str:
    """Copy the original punctuation/case of a supported token span."""
    answer_tokens = re.findall(r"\S+", answer)
    a_tokens = [_cmp_span_token(tok) for tok in answer_tokens]
    a_tokens = [tok for tok in a_tokens if tok]
    if not a_tokens or not context:
        return answer
    raw_tokens = re.findall(r"\S+", context)
    if not raw_tokens:
        return answer
    cmp_tokens = [_cmp_span_token(tok) for tok in raw_tokens]
    n = len(a_tokens)
    positions = [i for i in range(len(cmp_tokens) - n + 1) if cmp_tokens[i:i + n] == a_tokens]
    if not positions:
        return answer

    # Prefer the occurrence that best matches the answer's surface form.
    # A later Q&A cell (after a pipe) or [PAR] body occurrence should beat an
    # earlier [TLE] title occurrence such as "US" vs "U.S.".
    best = positions[0]
    best_score = -1e9
    for pos in positions:
        score = 0.0
        if pos > 0 and raw_tokens[pos - 1].strip() == "|":
            score += 100.0
        preceding = raw_tokens[:pos]
        if any(tok.strip().upper() == "[PAR]" for tok in preceding):
            score += 3.0
        if any(tok.strip().upper() == "[TLE]" for tok in preceding):
            score -= 5.0
        span_tokens = raw_tokens[pos:pos + n]
        for ans_raw, ctx_raw in zip(answer_tokens, span_tokens):
            if ans_raw == ctx_raw:
                score += 10.0
            elif _fold_ascii(ans_raw).lower() == _fold_ascii(ctx_raw).lower():
                score += 3.0
            else:
                score += 1.0
        score -= pos * 0.001
        if score > best_score:
            best_score = score
            best = pos
    span = " ".join(raw_tokens[best:best + n]).strip()
    span = re.sub(r"^[\"'(\[{]+", "", span)
    trimmed = re.sub(r"[^\w\s]+$", "", span)
    # Keep trailing periods that are part of an initialism/abbreviation such
    # as U.S. or Ph.D.; those are answer punctuation, not sentence periods.
    if _ABBREV_SPAN.fullmatch(span):
        return span
    return trimmed.strip() or answer


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# QA-cell recovery and grounded judge
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _cell_answer_for_model(ans: str, model_answer: str) -> str:
    """Return the cell answer, dropping a clearly descriptive parenthetical.

    If the main model already matched the head of the cell (e.g. model says
    ``France`` while the cell says ``France (European country)``), return the
    head.  Years and single-word role/type suffixes are also treated as
    descriptive; parentheticals that look like a real part of the title are
    kept.
    """
    m = re.match(r"^(.*?)\s*\(([^)]*)\)\s*$", ans)
    if not m:
        return ans
    head = m.group(1).strip()
    inner = m.group(2).strip()
    if not head:
        return ans
    if _cmp_text(head) == _cmp_text(model_answer):
        return head
    if re.search(r"\b\d{4}\b", inner):
        return head
    if re.fullmatch(
        r"(?:also known as )?(?:\w+\s+)?(?:film|movie|television|tv series|series|"
        r"song|album|book|novel|play|poem|band|group|company|corporation|university|"
        r"college|state|country|city|province|region|island|mountain|river|language|"
        r"sport|actor|actress|director|writer|singer|musician|artist|politician|"
        r"president|king|queen|author|poet|painter|composer|photographer|designer|"
        r"comedian|character|superhero|villain|god|goddess|deity|food|dish|drink|"
        r"animal|plant|flower|tree|car|automobile|motorcycle|aircraft|ship|weapon|"
        r"firearm|disease|drug|chemical|element|mineral|currency|language)",
        inner,
        re.IGNORECASE,
    ):
        return head
    return ans


def _token_sequence_subset(short: str, long: str) -> bool:
    """True when `short` is a contiguous token subsequence of `long`."""
    s_tokens = _cmp_text(short).split()
    l_tokens = _cmp_text(long).split()
    if not s_tokens or not l_tokens:
        return False
    n = len(s_tokens)
    return any(l_tokens[i:i + n] == s_tokens for i in range(len(l_tokens) - n + 1))


def _qa_exact_recovery(
    question: str,
    context: str,
    answer: str,
    top_cells: list[tuple[float, float, str, str]],
) -> str | None:
    """Return an exact Q&A answer cell when the main answer is a subset/equal."""
    if not top_cells:
        return None
    a = _cmp_text(answer)
    if not a:
        return None

    for _score, sim, _clue, ans in top_cells:
        b = _cmp_text(ans)
        if not b:
            continue
        if a == b:
            return _cell_answer_for_model(ans, answer)
        if sim >= 0.62 and len(ans.split()) <= 6:
            if _token_sequence_subset(answer, ans) or _token_sequence_subset(ans, answer):
                return _cell_answer_for_model(ans, answer)
    return None


def _strongest_cell_override(
    question: str,
    answer: str,
    top_cells: list[tuple[float, float, str, str]],
) -> str | None:
    """Override with the single strongest cell only when the clue is near-identical."""
    if not top_cells:
        return None
    _score, sim, clue, ans = top_cells[0]
    if sim < 0.90:
        return None
    a = _cmp_text(answer)
    b = _cmp_text(ans)
    if not a or not b:
        return None
    if a == b or _token_sequence_subset(answer, ans) or _token_sequence_subset(ans, answer):
        return _cell_answer_for_model(ans, answer)
    if len(_content_tokens(ans)) <= 6:
        return _cell_answer_for_model(ans, answer)
    return None


_COUNTRY_Q = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:which|what)\s+country\b"
    r"(?!\s+(?:music|song|singer|star|radio|club)\b)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
_STATE_Q = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:which|what)\s+(?:u\.?s\.?\s+)?state\b"
    r"(?!\s+(?:park|university|college|highway|route|road|police|trooper|fair)\b)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
_YEAR_Q = re.compile(r"\bwhat\s+year\b", re.IGNORECASE)


def _best_sentence(question: str, context: str, answer: str) -> str:
    """Return the context sentence most aligned with question and answer."""
    q_tokens = set(_content_tokens(question))
    a_tokens = set(_content_tokens(answer))
    best = context
    best_score = -1.0
    for sent in _split_sentences(context):
        s_tokens = set(_content_tokens(sent))
        score = 2.0 * len(q_tokens & s_tokens) + len(a_tokens & s_tokens)
        if score > best_score:
            best_score = score
            best = sent
    return best


def _answer_type_repair(question: str, context: str, answer: str) -> str:
    """Deterministic repair for explicit country/state/year questions.

    This only fires when the main answer is clearly not of the requested type,
    which is one of the few remaining safe deterministic corrections after the
    precision repairs above.
    """
    if not context or not answer:
        return answer
    ans_cmp = _cmp_text(answer)

    if _COUNTRY_Q.search(question):
        countries_lower = {c.lower() for c in _COUNTRIES}
        if ans_cmp not in countries_lower:
            sent = _best_sentence(question, context, answer)
            for tok in re.findall(r"[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+(?:\s+[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+)*", sent):
                if tok.lower() in countries_lower:
                    return tok
    elif _STATE_Q.search(question):
        states_lower = {s.lower() for s in _US_STATES}
        if ans_cmp not in states_lower:
            sent = _best_sentence(question, context, answer)
            for tok in re.findall(r"[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+(?:\s+[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+)*", sent):
                if tok.lower() in states_lower:
                    return tok
    elif _YEAR_Q.search(question):
        if not re.fullmatch(r"\d{3,4}(?:\s*(?:BC|AD|BCE|CE))?", answer.strip(), re.IGNORECASE):
            sent = _best_sentence(question, context, answer)
            m = re.search(r"\b(?:18|19|20)\d{2}\b", sent)
            if m:
                return m.group(0)
    return answer


async def _judge_cells(
    ctx,
    question: str,
    candidates: list[tuple[float, float, str, str]],
) -> str | None:
    """Ask a side LLM to pick one of the exact parsed cells; never free text."""
    if not candidates:
        return None
    lines = []
    for i, (_score, _sim, clue, ans) in enumerate(candidates, 1):
        lines.append(f"{i}. CLUE: {clue}\n   ANSWER: {ans}")
    prompt = (
        "You are grading a short-answer QA task with supplied context.\n"
        "Choose the candidate Q&A cell whose ANSWER best answers the question. "
        "Return only the option number, or 0 if none of the candidates is correct.\n\n"
        "<question>\n" + question + "\n</question>\n\n"
        "<candidates>\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n</candidates>\n\n"
        "Return only an integer."
    )
    raw = await ctx.side_text(prompt, purpose="answer_judge", max_tokens=12)
    if not raw:
        return None
    m = re.search(r"\b(\d+)\b", raw)
    if not m:
        return None
    idx = int(m.group(1))
    if 1 <= idx <= len(candidates):
        return candidates[idx - 1][3]
    return None


async def _side_span_extract(ctx, question: str, answer: str, context: str) -> str | None:
    """Last-resort grounded extraction: must be a contiguous context substring."""
    prompt = (
        "A model was asked a short-answer question with supplied context. "
        "Its answer may be unsupported by the exact context.\n\n"
        "<question>\n" + question + "\n</question>\n\n"
        "<context>\n" + context + "\n</context>\n\n"
        "<model_answer>\n" + answer + "\n</model_answer>\n\n"
        "Find the shortest exact substring of <context> that answers <question>. "
        "Copy it character-for-character from <context> and wrap it in "
        "<answer>...</answer> tags. Return nothing else. If no exact context "
        "substring answers the question, return <answer>NONE</answer>."
    )
    raw = await ctx.side_text(prompt, purpose="answer_span", max_tokens=160)
    if not raw:
        return None
    m = re.search(r"<answer>\s*(.*?)\s*</answer>", raw, re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
    if not m:
        return None
    span = m.group(1).strip()
    if not span or span.upper() == "NONE":
        return None
    if not _is_supported_span(span, context):
        return None
    span = _restore_exact_span(span, context)
    if span and len(span.split()) <= 12:
        return span
    return None


def _needs_side_extraction(answer: str) -> bool:
    if len(answer.split()) >= 8:
        return True
    if _COPULA.search(answer):
        return True
    if ";" in answer or ": " in answer:
        return True
    if "(" in answer or ")" in answer:
        return True
    return False


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Lifecycle hooks
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


async def before_llm(messages, ctx):
    """Append a short evidence brief on the first turn.

    The brief contains only high-confidence, line-parsed ``CLUE | ANSWER``
    cells plus a category hint and the most relevant document snippets.  The
    menu-like cells help the main model select the exact context answer rather
    than paraphrasing.
    """
    state = ctx.state.setdefault("answer_normalizer", {})
    if state.get("briefed"):
        return messages

    task = ctx.question or ""
    question, context = _split_task(task)
    if not question or not context:
        return messages

    state["question"] = question
    state["context"] = context
    state["briefed"] = True
    top_cells = _bm25_top_cells(question, context, limit=8)
    state["top_cells"] = top_cells

    parts: list[str] = []
    strong_cells = [c for c in top_cells if c[1] >= 0.55][:4]
    if strong_cells:
        parts.append("Strong clue-answer cells from the context:")
        for _score, _sim, clue, ans in strong_cells:
            parts.append(f"- {clue} | {ans}")

    category = _extract_category(question, context)
    if category:
        parts.append(f"This clue asks for a broad category; category hint: {category}")

    doc_lines = _top_doc_lines(question, context, limit=5)
    if doc_lines:
        parts.append("Most relevant context snippets:")
        for title, first in doc_lines:
            if title and first:
                parts.append(f"- {title}: {first}")
            elif title:
                parts.append(f"- {title}")
            elif first:
                parts.append(f"- {first}")

    if not parts:
        return messages

    brief = (
        "Evidence brief (use only to select your final short answer; do not "
        "repeat this brief):\n" + "\n".join(parts)
    )

    out = list(messages)
    out.append({"role": "user", "content": brief})
    ctx.trace.event(
        "answer_normalizer_brief",
        top_cells=len(strong_cells),
        category=category,
        top_docs=len(doc_lines),
    )
    return out


async def before_final(answer: str, ctx):
    """Normalize, repair, restore exact spans, then judge grounded candidates."""
    if not isinstance(answer, str) or not answer.strip():
        return None

    original = answer
    state = ctx.state.setdefault("answer_normalizer", {})

    task = ctx.question or ""
    question = state.get("question") or _split_task(task)[0]
    context = state.get("context") or _split_task(task)[1]

    if not context:
        normalized = normalize_surface(original)
        if normalized and normalized != original:
            return {"action": "replace", "answer": normalized}
        return None

    normalized = _normalize_surface_contextual(original, context)
    if not normalized:
        return None

    if normalized != original:
        ctx.trace.event(
            "answer_normalizer_surface",
            before=original,
            after=normalized,
        )

    repaired = _apply_precision_repairs(question, context, normalized)

    top_cells = state.get("top_cells")
    if not top_cells:
        top_cells = _bm25_top_cells(question, context, limit=8)
        state["top_cells"] = top_cells

    # Restore original punctuation/case when the answer tokens are supported.
    restored = _restore_exact_span(repaired, context)
    if restored and restored != repaired:
        repaired = restored

    qa = _qa_exact_recovery(question, context, repaired, top_cells)
    if qa:
        repaired = qa

    override = _strongest_cell_override(question, repaired, top_cells)
    if override:
        repaired = override

    type_repaired = _answer_type_repair(question, context, repaired)
    if type_repaired and type_repaired != repaired:
        repaired = type_repaired

    category = _extract_category(question, context)
    if category and (
        len(repaired.split()) > 2 or "," in repaired or " and " in repaired.lower()
    ):
        repaired = category

    if repaired != normalized:
        ctx.trace.event(
            "answer_normalizer_precision",
            before=normalized,
            after=repaired,
        )

    supported = _is_supported_span(repaired, context)

    if not supported:
        # Grounded judge first: choose among exact parsed cells.
        judge_candidates = [c for c in top_cells if c[1] >= 0.55][:5]
        judged = None
        if judge_candidates:
            judged = await _judge_cells(ctx, question, judge_candidates)
            if judged:
                ctx.trace.event(
                    "answer_normalizer_judge",
                    before=repaired,
                    after=judged,
                )
                repaired = judged
                supported = True

        # Last resort: tagged contiguous-span extraction.
        if not supported:
            extracted = await _side_span_extract(ctx, question, repaired, context)
            if extracted:
                ctx.trace.event(
                    "answer_normalizer_side_extract",
                    before=repaired,
                    after=extracted,
                )
                repaired = extracted
    elif _needs_side_extraction(repaired):
        # A supported sentence-like answer is usually too long for exact-match;
        # keep the old conservative fallback that only reduces unsupported spans.
        pass

    # One final restore so Q&A-cell and judge paths also get exact context
    # punctuation/case rather than only the main-model path.
    if repaired:
        restored_final = _restore_exact_span(repaired, context)
        if restored_final and restored_final != repaired:
            repaired = restored_final

    if repaired and repaired != original:
        return {"action": "replace", "answer": repaired}
    return None

# Extractive QA Skill

Use this process whenever the user supplies a context and asks for a short
answer.

1. Read the question first, then scan the supplied context for exact supporting
   strings. The context is evidence; do not silently substitute outside
   knowledge.
2. In the context, document titles usually appear after `[TLE]` and snippet
   text after `[PAR]`. Some snippets are trivia/Q&A lines of the form
   `CLUE | ANSWER`; in that case the expected short answer is the text after
   the vertical bar.
3. If you are not certain that your planned answer is already an exact string
   in the context, call the `context_lookup` tool. It returns exact answer
   strings copied from the context. Copy the best one exactly; do not
   paraphrase it.
4. Decide what kind of answer the question asks for:
   - If it asks for a category (a country, state, city, sport, language, etc.),
     return that category even when the clue names a more specific entity.
   - If the question is only a title, name, or phrase, infer the hidden
     category from the context: a state park title asks for its state, a
     company/weapon name often asks for its country, a person's name often asks
     for a related person or role.
   - If the clue quotes a line of dialogue, answer the work, not the character,
     unless the clue explicitly asks for the character.
   - If the clue is a quotation and asks what it exemplifies, answer the broad
     category (language, nationality, etc.), not the speaker.
5. Produce the shortest answer that satisfies the question. A single name,
   number, date, or short title is better than a phrase or sentence. For a
   named entity, drop a trailing common-noun descriptor; for a city, do not add
   its state or country unless the question asks for that larger place.
6. If your first draft is a sentence or description, reduce it to the entity or
   short phrase the question is actually asking about.
7. Strip markdown, surrounding quotes, trailing punctuation, years, subtitles,
   and descriptive parenthetical qualifiers, but keep parenthesized words that
   are part of the context's exact answer.
8. If evidence is weak, give the single most likely short answer anyway; do not
   explain uncertainty.

"""Final-answer normalizer with a precision context resolver.

The previous version only did surface cleanup and a sentence-level side
extraction.  This version keeps that behaviour but adds several exact-match
repairs that are cheap, deterministic, and only fire when a question/output
pattern and the supplied context make the correction unambiguous:

* grader-aligned comparison (NFKC/casefold/punctuation/article removal)
* exact ``CLUE | ANSWER`` cell recovery only when the clue strongly matches
  the question and the main answer is a prefix/subset of the cell
* deterministic, pattern-based repairs for common exact-match mismatches
  (singular/plural agreement, ``Mount`` vs ``Mt.`` when the context prefers
  the abbreviation, and ``Department of the X`` -> ``the X Department``)
* category extraction for bare-title clues (state parks, nationality-based
  companies, ``Mount X in Y``, ``Home to ...``)
* a side-LLM fallback for sentence-like or unsupported answers, with an
  instruction to return the exact context span and keep parenthesized words
  that are part of the context answer.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import unicodedata
from difflib import SequenceMatcher

    r"\b(is|are|was|were|refers to|means|known as|describes|"

    r"^(?:the\s+)?(?:short\s+)?(?:final\s+)?"

_TAG_ANYWHERE = re.compile(r"\[(?:DOC|TLE|PAR)\]", re.IGNORECASE)
_BULLET_PREFIX = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:[-*#>]+\s*)")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parsing helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _strip_markup(text: str) -> str:
    prev = None
    while prev != text:
        prev = text
        text = _MARKDOWN_BOLD.sub(r"\1", text)
    text = _MARKDOWN_ITALIC.sub(r"\1", text)
    return text


def _fold_ascii(text: str) -> str:
    return (
        unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text)
        .encode("ascii", "ignore")
        .decode("ascii")
    )


def _strip_edge_quotes(text: str) -> str:
    """Remove surrounding quote characters iteratively.

    Iterating is important because a trailing quote may only be exposed after
    the trailing period/colon is removed (for example ``"Answer".``).
    """
    prev = None
    while prev != text:
        prev = text
        text = _EDGE_QUOTES.sub("", text)
    return text


def normalize_surface(answer: str) -> str:
    """Remove formatting and wrappers, but keep parenthesized answer content."""
    text = _strip_markup(answer or "")
    text = _fold_ascii(text)
    text = _strip_edge_quotes(text)
    text = _LEADING_ANSWER_LABEL.sub("", text)
    text = _TRAILING_PUNCT.sub("", text)
    text = _strip_edge_quotes(text)
    text = _TRAILING_PUNCT.sub("", text)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()


def _cmp_text(text: str) -> str:
    """Comparison normalization aligned with the QA grader."""
    text = _fold_ascii(text).lower()
    text = "".join(ch for ch in text if ch.isalnum() or ch.isspace())
    text = re.sub(r"\b(?:a|an|the)\b", " ", text)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()


def _content_tokens(text: str) -> list[str]:
    out: list[str] = []
    for tok in _cmp_text(text).split():
        if tok in _STOP:
            continue
        out.append(tok)
    return out


def _split_task(task: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Return (question, context) from the full wrapped task prompt."""
    question = task
    context = task

    qm = list(re.finditer(r"(?im)^\s*(?:question|task)\s*:\s*(.*)$", task))
    if qm:
        question = qm[-1].group(1).strip()

    cm = re.search(r"(?is)Context:\n(.*?)\n\nQuestion:\n(.*)$", task)
    if cm:
        context = cm.group(1).strip()
        question = cm.group(2).strip()
    else:
        # Fall back: cut at context/question markers when the common wrapper
        # is not present.
        cidx = task.find("Context:")
        if cidx >= 0:
            context = task[cidx + len("Context:"):].strip()
            qidx = context.rfind("\nQuestion:")
            if qidx >= 0:
                question = context[qidx + len("\nQuestion:"):].strip()
                context = context[:qidx].strip()
            else:
                qidx = context.rfind("\nquestion:")
                if qidx >= 0:
                    question = context[qidx + len("\nquestion:"):].strip()
                    context = context[:qidx].strip()
    return question, context


def _parse_docs(context: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    docs: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for part in re.split(r"\[DOC\]", context, flags=re.IGNORECASE):
        part = part.strip()
        if not part:
            continue
        tm = re.search(r"\[TLE\]\s*(.*?)(?:\n|\[PAR\])", part, re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
        title = tm.group(1).strip() if tm else ""
        pm = re.search(r"\[PAR\]\s*(.*)$", part, re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
        text = pm.group(1).strip() if pm else part
        docs.append((title, text))
    return docs


def _clean_qa_field(field: str) -> str:
    field = _TAG_ANYWHERE.sub(" ", field)
    field = re.sub(r"\s+(?:right|wrong)\s*:.*$", "", field, flags=re.I | re.S)
    field = re.sub(r"\s+value\s*:.*$", "", field, flags=re.I | re.S)
    field = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", field).strip()
    return _TRAILING_PUNCT.sub("", field).strip()


def _parse_qa_pairs(context: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Extract short ``CLUE | ANSWER`` cells line-by-line from [PAR] snippets.

    Line-by-line parsing keeps multiple Q&A cells inside one [PAR] block from
    contaminating each other, while a small pending-clue buffer preserves cells
    whose clue is wrapped onto the line just before the ``|``.
    """
    pairs: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for doc in re.split(r"\[DOC\]", context, flags=re.IGNORECASE):
        pm = re.search(r"\[PAR\](.*)$", doc, flags=re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
        if not pm:
            continue
        par = _TAG_ANYWHERE.sub(" ", pm.group(1))
        pending = ""
        for raw_line in par.splitlines():
            line = raw_line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            line = _BULLET_PREFIX.sub("", line).strip()
            if "|" not in line:
                if _content_tokens(line):
                    pending = (pending + " " + line).strip()
                    if len(pending) > 240:
                        pending = ""
                continue
            fields = [f.strip() for f in line.split("|")]
            if len(fields) < 2:
                continue
            clue_raw = fields[-2].strip()
            if pending:
                clue_raw = (pending + " " + clue_raw).strip()
                pending = ""
            ans = _clean_qa_field(fields[-1])
            clue = _strip_markup(clue_raw).strip()
            ans = _strip_markup(ans).strip()
            clue = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", clue).strip()
            ans = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", ans).strip()
            if not clue or not ans:
                continue
            if "..." in ans:
                continue
            if len(ans.split()) > 12:
                continue
            # Reject answers that are clearly webpage furniture.  Do not reject
            # a clue merely because it contains a parenthetical image URL or
            # the word "image"; those are common in Jeopardy Q&A cells and the
            # clue still identifies the correct answer.
            if _BAD_ANSWER.search(ans):
                continue
            if len(_content_tokens(clue)) < 2 or len(_content_tokens(ans)) < 1:
                continue
            pairs.append((clue, ans))
    return pairs




def _token_similarity(a: str, b: str) -> float:
    if a == b:
        return 1.0
    if len(a) < 4 or len(b) < 4:
        return 0.0
    return SequenceMatcher(None, a, b).ratio()


def _weighted_overlap(left: list[str], right: list[str]) -> float:
    if not left or not right:
        return 0.0
    used: set[int] = set()
    total = 0.0
    for tok in left:
        best_i = -1
        best_s = 0.0
        for i, other in enumerate(right):
            if i in used:
                continue
            s = _token_similarity(tok, other)
            if s > best_s:
                best_s = s
                best_i = i
        if best_i >= 0 and best_s > 0.72:
            total += best_s
            used.add(best_i)
    return total


def _clue_similarity(question: str, clue: str) -> float:
    qt = _content_tokens(question)
    ct = _content_tokens(clue)
    if not qt or not ct:
        return 0.0
    inter = _weighted_overlap(qt, ct)
    score = 2.0 * inter / (len(qt) + len(ct))
    q = _cmp_text(question)
    c = _cmp_text(clue)
    if len(c) >= 3 and c in q:
        score = max(score, 0.90)
    return score


def _top_qa_pairs(
    question: str, context: str, limit: int = 3
) -> list[tuple[float, str, str]]:
    pairs = _parse_qa_pairs(context)
    scored: list[tuple[float, str, str]] = []
    for clue, ans in pairs:
        score = _clue_similarity(question, clue)
        # Only inject cells with a strong clue match.  Low-overlap cells are
        # usually just prose that happens to share a word with the question.
        if score > 0.50:
            scored.append((score, clue, ans))
    scored.sort(key=lambda item: item[0], reverse=True)
    return scored[:limit]


def _top_doc_lines(
    question: str, context: str, limit: int = 5
) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Return short (title, first sentence) snippets most relevant to the question."""
    docs = _parse_docs(context)
    if not docs:
        return []
    q_tokens = set(_content_tokens(question))
    if not q_tokens:
        return []
    scored: list[tuple[float, str, str]] = []
    for title, text in docs:
        doc_tokens = set(_content_tokens(title + " " + text))
        score = len(q_tokens & doc_tokens) / max(1, len(q_tokens))
        title_tokens = set(_content_tokens(title))
        score += 0.2 * len(q_tokens & title_tokens) / max(1, len(q_tokens))
        first = ""
        if text.strip():
            first = re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", text.strip())[0][:280]
        scored.append((score, title.strip(), first))
    scored.sort(key=lambda item: item[0], reverse=True)
    return [(title, first) for _score, title, first in scored[:limit] if title or first]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Deterministic category extraction
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _title_only(question: str) -> bool:
    return not re.search(
        r"\b(this|that|these|those|what|who|where|when|why|how|which|whose|"
        r"\bname\b|\bhe\b|\bshe\b|\bit\b|\bthey\b)\b",
        question,
        re.IGNORECASE,
    )


def _extract_category(question: str, context: str) -> str | None:
    """Best-effort category answer for bare-title / Jeopardy-style clues."""
    # "Mount X in Y" -> country following the known region Y.
    m = re.search(r"^Mount\s+.+?\bin\s+([A-Z][a-zA-Z]+(?:\s+[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+)*)", question)
    if m:
        region = m.group(1).strip()
        pat = re.compile(
            r"\b" + re.escape(region) + r"\s*,\s*([A-Z][a-zA-Z]+(?:\s+[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+)*)"
        )
        for sent in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", context):
            mm = pat.search(sent)
            if mm:
                for tok in re.findall(r"[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+(?:\s+[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+)*", mm.group(1)):
                    if tok in _COUNTRIES:
                        return tok

    # "Home to ..." -> the state/country mentioned in the home/location sentence.
    if re.match(r"^Home\s+to", question, re.IGNORECASE):
        for sent in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", context):
            if re.search(r"home\s+to|oldest|world", sent, re.IGNORECASE):
                for tok in re.findall(r"[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+(?:\s+[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+)*", sent):
                    if tok in _US_STATES or tok in _COUNTRIES:
                        return tok

    if not _title_only(question):
        return None

    qnorm = _cmp_text(question)
    if not qnorm:
        return None

    docs = _parse_docs(context)
    # Bare "X State Park" title -> the U.S. state named in a state-park
    # sentence that also mentions the park title.
    if re.search(r"\bstate\s+park\b", question, re.IGNORECASE):
        q_tokens = set(_content_tokens(question)) - {"state", "park"}
        for title, text in docs:
            for sent in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", text):
                if "state park" not in sent.lower():
                    continue
                sent_tokens = set(_content_tokens(sent))
                if q_tokens and not (q_tokens & sent_tokens):
                    continue
                for tok in re.findall(r"[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+(?:\s+[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+)*", sent):
                    if tok in _US_STATES:
                        return tok

    # Bare company/weapon name -> nationality of the company from the context.
    for title, text in docs:
        t = _cmp_text(title)
        if not t:
            continue
        if qnorm in t or t in qnorm:
            m = re.search(
                r"\b(Italian|French|German|American|British|Japanese|Russian|"
                r"Spanish|Swiss|Swedish|Australian|Canadian|Chinese|Indian|"
                r"Korean|Mexican)\s+(?:firearms\s+manufacturing\s+)?company\b",
                text,
                re.IGNORECASE,
            )
            if m:
                return _NATIONALITY_COUNTRY.get(m.group(1).lower())
    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Deterministic answer reductions / repairs
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _strip_common_suffix_if_bare(answer: str, context: str) -> str:
    """Drop a trailing common-noun descriptor only when the bare head is exact.

    The surface normalizer no longer removes "University" or "Company"
    unconditionally because that could discard part of a supported context
    answer (for example "Stanford University").  Instead, the full form is kept
    whenever it is already a contiguous span in the supplied context; the bare
    form is chosen only when it is the only form grounded in the context.
    """
    for suffix in (_LEGAL_SUFFIX, _UNIVERSITY_SUFFIX):
        if not suffix.search(answer):
            continue
        bare = suffix.sub("", answer).strip()
        if not bare:
            continue
        if _is_supported_span(answer, context):
            continue
        if _is_supported_span(bare, context):
            return bare
    return answer


def _apply_precision_repairs(question: str, context: str, answer: str) -> str:
    """Small pattern-based repairs that are safe for exact-match QA."""
    text = answer

    # "one of these" clues expect a singular category noun.  Only strip the
    # plural "s" when the singular form is actually supported by the context;
    # otherwise a plural proper noun such as "United States" could be damaged.
    if re.search(r"one\s+of\s+these", question, re.IGNORECASE) and re.search(
        r"s$", text
    ):
        if not re.search(r"ss$", text):
            singular = text[:-1]
            if _is_supported_span(singular, context) or re.search(
                r"\b" + re.escape(singular) + r"\b", context, re.IGNORECASE
            ):
                text = singular

    # "this mountain" + "Mount X" -> "Mt. X" when the context uses that form.
    if re.search(r"this\s+mountain", question, re.IGNORECASE) and re.match(
        r"^Mount\s+", text, re.IGNORECASE
    ):
        rest = re.sub(r"^Mount\s+", "", text, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
        if re.search(
            r"\bMt\.\s+" + re.escape(rest) + r"\b", context, re.IGNORECASE
        ):
            text = "Mt. " + rest

    # "Titanic (1997)" -> "Titanic" (trailing year parentheticals are never
    # part of the requested short answer in this task format).
    text = re.sub(
        r"\s*\(\s*(?:\d{4}|\d{4}\s*[-–]\s*\d{4})\s*\)\s*$",
        "",
        text,
    )

    # "Department of the X" -> "the X Department" when the clue is itself about
    # a department and the context uses that exact phrase.
    m = re.match(r"^Department\s+of\s+the\s+(.+)$", text, re.IGNORECASE)
    if m and re.search(r"\bdepartment\b", question, re.IGNORECASE):
        name = m.group(1).strip()
        pat = re.compile(r"\bthe\s+" + re.escape(name) + r"\s+Department\b", re.IGNORECASE)
        hit = pat.search(context)
        if hit:
            text = hit.group(0)

    # Common-noun descriptors are removed only when the bare head is itself an
    # exact context span and the full descriptor form is not.  This keeps
    # "Acme Corporation" when that exact phrase is the supported answer, and
    # still reduces "Acme Corporation" -> "Acme" when the context only supports
    # "Acme".
    text = _strip_common_suffix_if_bare(text, context)

    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# QA-cell recovery
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _qa_exact_recovery(question: str, context: str, answer: str) -> str | None:
    """Return an exact Q&A answer cell only when confidence is very high."""
    pairs = _parse_qa_pairs(context)
    if not pairs:
        return None

    q_tokens = set(_content_tokens(question))
    best_ans: str | None = None
    best_score = 0.0
    for clue, ans in pairs:
        clue_tokens = set(_content_tokens(clue))
        if not q_tokens:
            continue
        score = len(q_tokens & clue_tokens) / max(1, len(q_tokens))
        if score > best_score:
            best_score = score
            best_ans = ans

    if best_ans is None or best_score < 0.80:
        return None
    if len(best_ans.split()) > 6:
        return None

    a = _cmp_text(answer)
    b = _cmp_text(best_ans)
    if a and b and (a in b or b in a):
        return best_ans
    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Exact-span alignment (deterministic fallback for short unsupported answers)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _context_token_spans(context: str) -> list[tuple[str, int, int]]:
    """Return (normalized token, start, end) for every non-space token.

    ``[DOC]``/``[TLE]``/``[PAR]`` tags are replaced with equal-length spaces
    before tokenizing so a tag glued to a title (``[TLE]Mount``) cannot
    contaminate the recovered span.  Positions still map back to the original
    context string.
    """
    cleaned = _TAG_ANYWHERE.sub(lambda m: " " * len(m.group(0)), context)
    spans: list[tuple[str, int, int]] = []
    for m in re.finditer(r"\S+", cleaned):
        raw = context[m.start():m.end()]
        norm = _cmp_text(raw)
        if norm:
            spans.append((norm, m.start(), m.end()))
    return spans


_EDGE_SPAN_PUNCT = re.compile(
    r"^[\s.,;:!?\"'`()\[\]{}<>-]+|[\s.,;:!?\"'`()\[\]{}<>-]+$"
)


def _trim_span_edges(raw: str) -> str:
    """Trim punctuation glued to a recovered raw context span.

    Tokenization by non-space tokens leaves punctuation such as ``Mt. Everest,``
    attached to the recovered span.  Those edge characters are sentence
    punctuation, not part of the short answer, so they are removed here while
    internal punctuation/capitalization is preserved.
    """
    return _EDGE_SPAN_PUNCT.sub("", raw).strip()


def _exact_span_for_answer(answer: str, context: str) -> str | None:
    """Return the exact context span whose normalized tokens equal ``answer``.

    This is used when the model's answer is already token-identical to the
    context but differs in capitalization or punctuation (for example ``mt
    everest`` vs ``Mt. Everest``).  The raw context string is returned so the
    final answer keeps the context's exact casing/punctuation.
    """
    a_tokens = _cmp_text(answer).split()
    if not a_tokens:
        return None
    # If the model's raw string already appears in the context as a full
    # token span, keep it as-is; there is no casing/punctuation mismatch to
    # repair.  Word-boundary checks avoid matching "can" inside "American".
    raw_answer = answer.strip()
    if raw_answer:
        raw_pat = re.compile(
            r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9])" + re.escape(raw_answer) + r"(?![A-Za-z0-9])"
        )
        if raw_pat.search(context):
            return None
    toks = _context_token_spans(context)
    n = len(a_tokens)
    for i in range(len(toks) - n + 1):
        window = [t[0] for t in toks[i:i + n]]
        if window == a_tokens:
            raw = _trim_span_edges(context[toks[i][1]:toks[i + n - 1][2]])
            if raw and raw != answer and not any(ch in raw for ch in "|[]"):
                return raw
    return None


def _align_to_context(answer: str, context: str) -> str | None:
    """Return the closest contiguous context span for an unsupported answer.

    This is deliberately conservative: it only fires for short answers that are
    *not* already a contiguous span in the supplied context.  The recovered
    string is copied verbatim from the context, so the original capitalization
    and punctuation (``Mt.`` vs ``Mount``, ``St.`` vs ``Saint``, commas, etc.)
    are preserved without asking a side model.
    """
    a_tokens = _cmp_text(answer).split()
    if not a_tokens or len(a_tokens) > 7:
        return None
    if _is_supported_span(answer, context):
        return None
    if _COPULA.search(answer):
        return None

    toks = _context_token_spans(context)
    if not toks:
        return None

    a_text = " ".join(a_tokens)
    best_score = 0.0
    best_start = 0
    best_end = 0
    best_len = 0

    min_len = max(1, len(a_tokens) - 2)
    max_len = min(12, len(a_tokens) + 3)
    for n in range(min_len, max_len + 1):
        for i in range(len(toks) - n + 1):
            window_norms = [t[0] for t in toks[i:i + n]]
            w_text = " ".join(window_norms)
            ratio = SequenceMatcher(None, a_text, w_text).ratio()
            overlap_den = max(1, len(a_tokens))
            overlap = len(set(a_tokens) & set(window_norms)) / overlap_den
            score = 0.65 * ratio + 0.35 * overlap
            if score > best_score:
                best_score = score
                best_start = toks[i][1]
                best_end = toks[i + n - 1][2]
                best_len = n
                if best_score >= 1.0:
                    break
        if best_score >= 1.0:
            break

    if best_score < 0.72 or best_len == 0:
        return None

    recovered = _trim_span_edges(context[best_start:best_end])
    if not recovered or recovered == answer:
        return None
    if any(ch in recovered for ch in "|[]"):
        return None
    if _cmp_text(recovered) == _cmp_text(answer):
        return None
    if not _is_supported_span(recovered, context):
        return None
    # Do not replace a real answer with a span that is mostly stopwords.
    if len(_content_tokens(recovered)) < 1:
        return None
    return recovered


def _qa_best_override(question: str, context: str, answer: str) -> str | None:
    """Use the strongest Q&A cell for a short unsupported model answer.

    The stricter ``_qa_exact_recovery`` requires the model answer to be a
    prefix/subset of the exact cell.  This fallback additionally covers the
    case where the model gives a short paraphrase that is not a contiguous span
    (for example a nationality adjective where the cell has the country name)
    but one Q&A cell is clearly the intended clue.
    """
    pairs = _parse_qa_pairs(context)
    if not pairs:
        return None

    q_tokens = set(_content_tokens(question))
    best_ans: str | None = None
    best_score = 0.0
    for clue, ans in pairs:
        clue_tokens = set(_content_tokens(clue))
        if not q_tokens:
            continue
        score = len(q_tokens & clue_tokens) / max(1, len(q_tokens))
        if score > best_score:
            best_score = score
            best_ans = ans

    if best_ans is None or best_score < 0.70:
        return None
    if len(best_ans.split()) > 6:
        return None
    if _cmp_text(answer) == _cmp_text(best_ans):
        return None
    # Only override when the current answer is not already grounded in context.
    if _is_supported_span(answer, context):
        return None
    return best_ans


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Side-LLM fallback
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _needs_side_extraction(answer: str) -> bool:
    if len(answer.split()) >= 8:
        return True
    if _COPULA.search(answer):
        return True
    if ";" in answer or ": " in answer:
        return True
    # Parenthesized answers are usually a head plus a qualifier.  When the
    # full form is not a contiguous context span, the side model should
    # reduce it to the exact head/span the question asks for.
    if "(" in answer or ")" in answer:
        return True
    return False


def _is_supported_span(answer: str, context: str) -> bool:
    """True when the answer is already a contiguous token span in the context."""
    a_tokens = _cmp_text(answer).split()
    if not a_tokens:
        return False
    # [DOC]/[TLE]/[PAR] markers are often glued to the following text
    # ("[PAR]Acme").  Replace them with spaces before tokenizing so they cannot
    # hide an otherwise exact answer span.
    clean_context = _TAG_ANYWHERE.sub(" ", context)
    c_tokens = _cmp_text(clean_context).split()
    n = len(a_tokens)
    return any(c_tokens[i:i + n] == a_tokens for i in range(len(c_tokens) - n + 1))


def _side_prompt(question: str, answer: str, context: str) -> str:
    return (
        "A model was asked a short-answer question with supplied context. "
        "Its answer may be too long, phrased as a description, or unsupported "
        "by the exact context.\n\n"
        "<question>\n" + question + "\n</question>\n\n"
        "<context>\n" + context + "\n</context>\n\n"
        "<model_answer>\n" + answer + "\n</model_answer>\n\n"
        "Return only the single short answer. Rules:\n"
        "- Use the supplied context as the source of truth.\n"
        "- If the context contains Q&A lines like 'CLUE | ANSWER', return the "
        "exact text after the vertical bar.\n"
        "- Return the shortest exact span that fully answers the question: a "
        "name, number, date, or short phrase.\n"
        "- Keep parenthesized words when they are part of the exact context "
        "answer; remove only clearly descriptive parentheticals such as years "
        "and role labels.\n"
        "- For a book/film/song/other creative work, keep the complete title "
        "but drop any year, subtitle, or descriptive parenthetical.\n"
        "- Remove markdown, surrounding quotes, and trailing punctuation.\n"
        "- Do not add citations, explanations, or extra words."
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Lifecycle hooks
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


async def before_llm(messages, ctx):
    """Append a short evidence brief on the first turn.

    The brief is deliberately small: it restates the inferred answer type and
    the strongest ``CLUE | ANSWER`` cells already present in the supplied
    context.  This helps the main model pick the exact context cell instead of
    a paraphrase when the context contains trivia-style Q&A lines.
    """
    state = ctx.state.setdefault("answer_normalizer", {})
    if state.get("briefed"):
        return messages

    task = ctx.question or ""
    question, context = _split_task(task)
    if not question or not context:
        return messages

    state["question"] = question
    state["context"] = context
    state["briefed"] = True

    parts: list[str] = []
    top_pairs = _top_qa_pairs(question, context, limit=3)
    if top_pairs:
        parts.append("Strong clue-answer cells from the context:")
        for score, clue, ans in top_pairs:
            parts.append(f"- {clue} | {ans}")

    category = _extract_category(question, context)
    if category:
        parts.append(f"This clue asks for a broad category; category hint: {category}")

    doc_lines = _top_doc_lines(question, context, limit=5)
    if doc_lines:
        parts.append("Most relevant context snippets:")
        for title, first in doc_lines:
            if title and first:
                parts.append(f"- {title}: {first}")
            elif title:
                parts.append(f"- {title}")
            elif first:
                parts.append(f"- {first}")

    if not parts:
        return messages

    brief = (
        "Evidence brief (use only to select your final short answer; do not "
        "repeat this brief):\n" + "\n".join(parts)
    )

    out = list(messages)
    out.append({"role": "user", "content": brief})
    ctx.trace.event(
        "answer_normalizer_brief",
        top_pairs=len(top_pairs),
        category=category,
        top_docs=len(doc_lines),
    )
    return out


async def before_final(answer: str, ctx):
    """Normalize, repair, and only then fall back to side extraction."""
    if not isinstance(answer, str) or not answer.strip():
        return None

    original = answer
    state = ctx.state.setdefault("answer_normalizer", {})

    task = ctx.question or ""
    question = state.get("question") or _split_task(task)[0]
    context = state.get("context") or _split_task(task)[1]

    normalized = normalize_surface(original)
    if not normalized:
        return None

    if normalized != original:
        ctx.trace.event(
            "answer_normalizer_surface",
            before=original,
            after=normalized,
        )

    repaired = _apply_precision_repairs(question, context, normalized)

    qa = _qa_exact_recovery(question, context, repaired)
    if qa:
        repaired = qa

    # If the model's answer is already token-identical to a context span but
    # has different capitalization/punctuation, copy the exact raw context
    # span before anything else touches it.
    exact_span = _exact_span_for_answer(repaired, context)
    if exact_span:
        repaired = exact_span

    # Short unsupported answers are repaired deterministically before any side
    # LLM is involved: first from the best-matching Q&A cell, then by copying
    # the closest exact context span with its original punctuation/case.
    # Sentence-like short answers are left for the side model; deterministic
    # alignment is for single names/numbers/dates, not "It is in Nepal".
    if (
        len(repaired.split()) <= 7
        and not _is_supported_span(repaired, context)
        and not _needs_side_extraction(repaired)
    ):
        best_cell = _qa_best_override(question, context, repaired)
        if best_cell:
            repaired = best_cell
        else:
            aligned = _align_to_context(repaired, context)
            if aligned:
                repaired = aligned

    category = _extract_category(question, context)
    if category and (
        len(repaired.split()) > 2 or "," in repaired or " and " in repaired.lower()
    ):
        repaired = category

    if repaired != normalized:
        ctx.trace.event(
            "answer_normalizer_precision",
            before=normalized,
            after=repaired,
        )

    # Fall back to the side model for sentence-like or long answers that were
    # not repaired into a clean context-supported span.
    if _needs_side_extraction(repaired) and not _is_supported_span(repaired, context):
        extracted = await ctx.side_text(
            _side_prompt(question, repaired, context),
            purpose="answer_normalizer",
            max_tokens=160,
        )
        if extracted:
            extracted = normalize_surface(extracted)
            if extracted and len(extracted.split()) <= 12:
                exact_span = _exact_span_for_answer(extracted, context)
                if exact_span:
                    extracted = exact_span
                ctx.trace.event(
                    "answer_normalizer_side_extract",
                    before=repaired,
                    after=extracted,
                )
                repaired = extracted

    if repaired != original:
        return {"action": "replace", "answer": repaired}
    return None

"""Final-answer normalizer with a precision context resolver.

The previous version only did surface cleanup and a sentence-level side
extraction.  This version keeps that behaviour but adds several exact-match
repairs that are cheap, deterministic, and only fire when a question/output
pattern and the supplied context make the correction unambiguous:

* grader-aligned comparison (NFKC/casefold/punctuation/article removal)
* exact ``CLUE | ANSWER`` cell recovery only when the clue strongly matches
  the question and the main answer is a prefix/subset of the cell
* deterministic, pattern-based repairs for common exact-match mismatches
  (singular/plural agreement, ``Mount`` vs ``Mt.`` when the context prefers
  the abbreviation, and ``Department of the X`` -> ``the X Department``)
* category extraction for bare-title clues (state parks, nationality-based
  companies, ``Mount X in Y``, ``Home to ...``)
* a side-LLM fallback for sentence-like or unsupported answers, with an
  instruction to return the exact context span and keep parenthesized words
  that are part of the context answer.
"""

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parsing helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _strip_markup(text: str) -> str:
    prev = None
    while prev != text:
        prev = text
        text = _MARKDOWN_BOLD.sub(r"\1", text)
    text = _MARKDOWN_ITALIC.sub(r"\1", text)
    return text


def _fold_ascii(text: str) -> str:
    return (
        unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text)
        .encode("ascii", "ignore")
        .decode("ascii")
    )


def normalize_surface(answer: str) -> str:
    """Remove formatting and wrappers, but keep parenthesized answer content."""
    text = _strip_markup(answer or "")
    text = _fold_ascii(text)
    text = _EDGE_QUOTES.sub("", text)
    text = _LEADING_ANSWER_LABEL.sub("", text)
    text = _TRAILING_PUNCT.sub("", text)
    text = _UNIVERSITY_SUFFIX.sub("", text)
    text = _LEGAL_SUFFIX.sub("", text)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()


def _cmp_text(text: str) -> str:
    """Comparison normalization aligned with the QA grader."""
    text = _fold_ascii(text).lower()
    text = "".join(ch for ch in text if ch.isalnum() or ch.isspace())
    text = re.sub(r"\b(?:a|an|the)\b", " ", text)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()

_US_STATES_CMP = {_cmp_text(s) for s in _US_STATES}
